check_service_status.description: Check whether the Official Joke API is answering, and how quickly. This is the one action that reports a problem as a value instead of failing the step, so a workflow can decide what to do about it. Being rate limited is reported separately from being down, since the service allows 100 requests every 15 minutes per address.

mock_response.message: The Official Joke API is up and answering.

check_service_status.name: check_service_status

get_joke_by_id.description: Get one specific joke by its id, for re-reading a joke an earlier step found. Ids are positions in the service's joke file and are handed out when it restarts, so a joke inserted upstream shifts every id after it: store the joke itself, not its id, if it has to still mean the same thing next month.

joke.punchline: He's adept at riffing in C#.
joke.setup: Why would a guitarist become a good programmer?
joke.text:
Why would a guitarist become a good programmer?
He's adept at riffing in C#.

get_joke_by_id.name: get_joke_by_id

parameters.description: The joke's numeric id. A full official-joke-api.appspot.com joke URL is also accepted.
parameters.name: joke_id

get_joke_from_rotation.description: Tell a different joke every day, week or month without ever repeating one too soon. The jokes are laid out once in a shuffled order and the rotation moves one place along it each day, week or month, so no joke comes round again until every other joke has been told. The joke of the day picks afresh each day and repeats itself within weeks; this does not. The same day always gives the same joke, so a retry or a second run tells the same one, and nothing has to be remembered between runs. Add a seed of your own to have two workspaces work through the jokes in different orders.
get_joke_from_rotation.display_name: Get a joke from a rotation
get_joke_from_rotation.display_str_template: Get the joke from the rotation for {0}.

joke.punchline: Because it's bitter like their code.
joke.setup: Why do programmers prefer dark chocolate?
joke.text:
Why do programmers prefer dark chocolate?
Because it's bitter like their code.

get_joke_from_rotation.name: get_joke_from_rotation

parameters.description: The day to get the joke for. Leave empty for today in UTC, which is what a scheduled step wants.
parameters.name: date

parameters.description: How often the rotation moves on to its next joke. A weekly rotation changes on Mondays and a monthly one on the 1st, so every run in between tells the same joke.
parameters.name: changes_every

parameters.description: Only return jokes of this type, or of any of several types separated by commas, such as 'general, dad'. The service publishes general, programming, knock-knock and dad; run Get joke types for the current list. Leave empty to draw from every joke.
parameters.name: joke_type

parameters.description: Any text you like. It decides the order the jokes are told in, so two workspaces with different seeds tell different jokes on the same day. Leave empty to share the order with everyone else. Changing it starts a new order, which may tell a recent joke again.
parameters.name: seed

get_joke_of_the_day.description: Pick one joke for a day and keep picking that same joke all day. A random draw gives a different joke on every call, so a daily workflow that retries, or that two people run an hour apart, tells two different jokes for the one day. This one is fixed by the date: the same date always gives the same joke, and tomorrow gives a different one. Add a seed of your own to have two workspaces tell different jokes on the same day.
get_joke_of_the_day.display_name: Get the joke of the day
get_joke_of_the_day.display_str_template: Get the joke of the day for {0}.

joke.setup: What did the fish say when it hit the wall?
joke.text:
What did the fish say when it hit the wall?
Dam.

parameters.description: Any text you like, mixed into the day so that two workspaces running this on the same day get different jokes. Leave empty to share the day's joke with everyone else.

get_random_jokes.description: Get several different jokes at once, up to 100, optionally all of one type. No joke is drawn twice in the same batch. Give it a seed and the same seed draws the same jokes in the same order every time, so a run can be repeated; leave the seed empty for a fresh draw. Asking for more jokes of a type than exist returns all of them rather than failing.

list_joke_types.description: List the joke types the service currently publishes and how many jokes each one holds, biggest first, so a step that filters by type knows what it can ask for and how much there is to draw on.
list_joke_types.name: list_joke_types

list_jokes.description: Page through every joke in the catalogue in a fixed order, optionally only of one type or of several. A random draw gives different jokes each time; this gives the same jokes for the same page, so a workflow can copy the whole catalogue into a sheet or a table a page at a time, reading the next offset off each page until there are no more. The service has no list of its own, so this reads its whole catalogue and pages through it here.

search_jokes.description: Find jokes about something: search every setup and punchline for a word or phrase, best match first. A joke matches on the whole phrase, or on all of your words appearing somewhere in it, and each result says whether the match was in the setup or the punchline. The service has no search of its own, so this reads its whole catalogue and matches here.

parameters.description: How many matches to return, from 1 to 100. Defaults to 10. The total number of matches is always reported, however many are returned.

description: Pull jokes from the Official Joke API's open catalogue of several hundred setups and punchlines. Draw one at random or a batch of them, narrow to a type such as programming, knock-knock or dad or to several at once, search every joke for a subject, look one up by id, page through the whole catalogue, pick a joke of the day that stays the same all day so a scheduled post never tells two, or work through a rotation that tells every joke before it repeats one.
